newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes fall as traders talk imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes fall as traders talk imports.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes ended the day lower with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Tuesday, while local refiners continued to deal in foreign cargoes, leaving Alaskan discounts flat.
Traders said a bomb threat at a nearby building kept some BP traders away from their office in Long Beach, Calif., Tuesday. Trading operations were not disrupted.
Buyers said a large refiner was asking $1.20 a barrel for late April barrels of Ecudorian Oriente. The barrels, part of larger cargo, would precede two full cargoes due in May.
The offers followed Exxon's sale a 400,000 barrel cargo of ANS to the refiner on Friday. The price, $1.32 off May WTI, is 0.27-cent widening from the last deal.
Outright prices stood at $18.18/18.38 a barrel, a 30-cent decrease from Monday.
A leading seller of ANS priced shipments at $0.95 cents under WTI.
ARCO, normally a seller of Wilmington crude, looked to buy the grade for May as their production slipped. The grade, rarely traded on the spot market, was rpiced 75 to 85 cents over postings.
Line 63 and California heavy crude markets remained well- supplied, with no deals reported Monday or Tuesday.
